heroLead: Coal Center earned its name honestly, and the deeds that came out of the coal era here still shape who owns what underground along this stretch of the Monongahela.
intro: Small river villages like Coal Center have a mineral ownership history that's easy to get wrong if you only think about Marcellus. Coal companies were buying and severing rights along the Mon River more than a century before horizontal shale drilling arrived, and that means a Coal Center deed can reference coal, oil, and gas as three completely separate estates, sometimes owned by three different families today.

If you've received something in the mail about a Coal Center-area interest and aren't sure what you actually hold, we can help sort that out and make you a direct cash offer for whatever piece is genuinely yours.

sections.heading: River Village, Layered Ownership
paragraphs: Coal Center sits right on the Monongahela, and river-adjacent land in this stretch of Washington County was some of the earliest to be developed for coal mining. That mining history means severed mineral estates are the rule here, not the exception. Oil and gas rights were often carved out separately from coal, and in some cases carved out again when Marcellus leasing arrived decades later.
Sorting out which layer you own, and whether it's still yours or was sold off by a prior generation, is exactly the kind of title work we do before ever discussing a number.

sections.heading: When the Well Isn't Even in Coal Center
paragraphs: Drilling units don't respect small-village boundaries. A Coal Center mineral interest can be pooled into a unit whose surface wellsite sits in a neighboring township entirely, which can be confusing if you're trying to match your royalty statement to a well you've never actually seen. That's normal, and it doesn't mean anything's wrong. We can help you match your statement to the actual unit it belongs to.

sections.heading: A Straightforward Cash Offer, No Broker
paragraphs: We buy mineral and royalty interests directly from owners, which means there's no broker fee eating into what you receive and no waiting for a buyer to be found on some listing site. For a small river-village interest like a lot of what we see near Coal Center, that directness usually matters more to families than chasing the last possible dollar through a drawn-out process.

faqs.question: My deed near Coal Center only mentions coal. Could I still own gas rights?
faqs.answer: Possibly not, if the coal, oil, and gas were severed into separate estates, which was common in this area. We check the full chain of title to be sure.

faqs.question: My royalty statement references a well I've never heard of. Is that normal?
faqs.answer: Yes. Drilling units can extend beyond a village's boundaries, so your interest may be pooled into a unit whose wellsite sits elsewhere.

faqs.question: How is selling to you different from listing my interest with a broker?
faqs.answer: We buy directly, so there's no broker commission and no waiting for a buyer to show up. You deal with us start to finish.
